clue.text: Shaky cover provided around City area

indicators.note: the word for cover is placed around the City letters, wrapping them

parts.note: to insure is to provide cover against loss
EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: An insurance policy feels flimsy when it only extends to one part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, capitalised, is London's financial square mile, whose postal district begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unstable or not firmly fixed, as a shaky structure is.

clue.text: Aggravate trendy sweetheart

parts.note: in fashion, so IN
an old flame is a former lover, so a flame is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A fashionable new partner is causing irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame a situation is to make it worse, a synonym for aggravate.

clue.text: Small insect, a visitor in December

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A tiny bug comes calling at Christmas time.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas calls on households on Christmas Eve, so he is a seasonal visitor.

clue.text: Talk with woman custodian of castle

parts.note: an informal talk is a chat
Elaine is a woman's name, as in the Arthurian lady

explanation.surface: A conversation with a lady who keeps watch over a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is historically the mistress of a large house or castle, holding its keys.

clue.text: Brought up — or torn down, do we hear?

indicators.note: asks whether we are hearing a word spoken, so the answer sounds like the word for torn down

parts.note: a building razed has been demolished

explanation.surface: A question over whether something was erected or demolished, a neat pair of opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are opposites in meaning yet identical in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a child is to bring them up, so brought up is a synonym.

clue.text: Do the bidding of old Turkish governor

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a district in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: Following the orders of a former Ottoman official.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey someone is to carry out their commands, which is what doing their bidding means.

clue.text: Pirate's gear adopted by gang

indicators.note: taken in by, so the gear word sits inside the gang word

parts.note: a band is a group of people, such as a gang
rig is equipment or kit

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's equipment is taken over by a criminal crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or robber, so a pirate is a sea-going version of the same outlaw.

clue.text: The old way to secure a baker's requisite

indicators.note: the two outer pieces together hold the a fast between them

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned route to getting what a baker needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough needs a raising agent, and this fungus is the one bakers traditionally use.

clue.text: Disney film buff beginning to tour vast continent

parts.note: an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word, so only its first letter

parts.note: only its opening letter is used
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A film enthusiast starts a tour of a huge landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 animated feature from the Walt Disney studio set to classical music.

clue.text: Pass one's required to visit Virginia

indicators.note: the one letter must go inside the state abbreviation, visiting it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and the 's is read as is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a permit to enter an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as one is: I plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official document allowing entry to a country, a kind of pass.

clue.text: Unkempt educationalist teased about leggings, principally

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

indicators.note: the word for teased goes round the leggings letter

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

indicators.note: first and foremost, so the first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A teacher looks scruffy after being mocked over their leggings.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd, Bachelor of Education, stands in for a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bedraggled looks untidy and dishevelled, a synonym for unkempt.

clue.text: Gemstone of silver polished off

parts.note: to polish off food is to eat it all, so ate

explanation.surface: A gem made of silver has been given a shine.
explanation.walkthrough: AG is the chemical symbol for silver. Polished off looks like buffing a stone but means eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony prized as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Stylish English worker welcoming support

indicators.note: taking a guest in, so the English worker pair holds the support word

parts.note: the worker ant is the usual crossword worker
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A well-dressed English labourer opens the door to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Trick scatty parent

indicators.note: scatterbrained and disorganised, so the letters of parent are jumbled

parts.note: its six letters are the fodder that gets rearranged

explanation.surface: A disorganised mother or father is fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to deceive them into a trap, a synonym for trick as a verb.

clue.text: More pungent-smelling Moroccan port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having a sharper odour, the comparative of tangy
second meaning: the city on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: A North African harbour town with a sharper smell than most.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of tangy has the same letters as the North African city opposite Gibraltar.

clue.text: Wedding bouquet's first delivered by little Albert

indicators.note: the bouquet's first means just its opening letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
to be delivered from something is to be rid of it
Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A wedding bouquet is handed over by a young boy called Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivered suggests handing over flowers but here means freed, as in rid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal means relating to a bride or a marriage ceremony, as wedding does when used before a noun.

clue.text: Put before duke, arranged in tiers

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something set down in front of a nobleman, stacked in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Before looks like a positional instruction but supplies the old word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something layered is built up in successive levels, like the tiers of a cake.

clue.text: Magnate's time over there securing company

indicators.note: holding firm, so the over-there word wraps the company letters

parts.note: yon is an old word meaning that, over there

explanation.surface: A business baron's moment over yonder, landing a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful businessperson, the same as a magnate.

clue.text: Extremely tractable girl's period as leaseholder

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only its outer letters are used
Nancy is a girl's name; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A very compliant young woman's time renting a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the occupation of property under a lease, or the length of time it lasts.

clue.text: Singer delivering note on radio

indicators.note: broadcast and heard rather than seen, so the answer sounds like the note word

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A vocalist hitting a musical note on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Note suggests music but is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with the highest natural adult voice in the standard range.

clue.text: Bloke eating very soft fish

indicators.note: taking food in, so the bloke word goes round the soft letters

parts.note: a guy is a man, a bloke
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A man is consuming some very tender fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The guppy is a small, brightly coloured tropical freshwater species kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Women's organisation feeding favourite shore bird

indicators.note: going in like food, so the women's group sits inside the favourite word

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation

explanation.surface: A women's club gives food to a beloved coastal bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit, or lapwing, is a plover found on farmland and coastal marshes.

clue.text: Arrest felon at last, and be sick

indicators.note: at the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: only its last letter is used
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A criminal is finally caught and feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is informal for catching and arresting them.

clue.text: Supporter of lupins initially in bloom

indicators.note: the lupins letter goes inside the bloom word

parts.note: a bloom is a flower

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so only the opening letters of of and lupins

parts.note: only the first letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: A fan of a garden plant with spires of pea-like blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: Initially applies to both of and lupins, not just the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower is an adherent or fan, someone who backs a cause, as a supporter does.

clue.text: Only lightly cooked? That's not common

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of meat, seared but red inside

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a steak; the second phrase is a separate sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes underdone steak and also anything scarce or unusual.

clue.text: New Etude in D not prepared for publication

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh musical study in the key of D that has not yet been revised for print.
explanation.walkthrough: An étude is a short study piece for an instrument, and D reads as a musical key.
